svg.title: What an FT8 transmission is
svg.text: One FT8 transmission: 15 s slot, 79 symbols, 8 tones
A · The 15-second slot (every :00, :15, :30, :45 by the clock)
Two stations take turns: one transmits in the even slots, the other in the odd ones. A QSO takes four to six slots; the decoder only has to read each slot.
B · Inside the transmission: three sync blocks and two data blocks
58 data symbols × 3 bits = 174 coded bits = 77 message bits + 14 CRC bits + 83 LDPC parity bits
C · Eight tones, 6.25 Hz apart (50 Hz in all)
The Costas pattern never repeats a tone and never repeats a step,
so it only lines up with itself at one exact time and frequency.
That is what the Sync Search looks for, three times per transmission.
Each data symbol sends 3 bits as one of the 8 tones (Gray code):
Neighbouring tones differ by one bit, so a tone read one step off costs one bit, not three.
Bandwidth 50 Hz, 6.25 baud, GFSK (smoothed) tone changes. Dozens of these fit side by side
in a radio's 3 kHz passband, and that is exactly what the decoder has to untangle.
